```{r}

#Add July month with sales revenue 17 to the plot and change the fill colour to green
barchart_data <- c(10, 15, 20, 5, 17) 
barchart_labels <- c("Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "July") 
print(barplot(barchart_data, names.arg=barchart_labels, xlab="Month", ylab="Sales Revenue", col="green", main ="Revenue chart", border="blue") )

```
```{r}
# Add x label as "Sales Revenue" and y label as " Month"
barplot(barchart_data, names.arg=barchart_labels, xlab="Sales Revenue", ylab= "Month", col="red", main ="Revenue chart", border="blue", horiz=TRUE) 

```

```{r}
# Move the legend to topleft and make the stacked chart vertical
 
colors = c("green","orange","brown")
months <- c("Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul") 
regions <- c("East","West","North") # Create the matrix of the values. 
Values <- matrix(c(2,9,3,11,9,4,8,7,3,12,5,2,8,10,11), nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE) 

# Create the stacked bar chart 
barplot(Values, main = "Sales Revenue", names.arg = months, xlab = "Revenue", ylab = "Month", col = colors) 
legend("topleft", regions, cex = 1.3, fill = colors)
```
```{r}
#Add Nova Scotia (NS) to the list of provinces with sales value 12 and add a label to the chart "Sales by Province"
library(ggplot2) 
slices <- c(10, 15, 10, 5, 8, 12) 
labels <- c("ON","QUE", "SK", "MAN", "BC", "NS") 
pie(slices, labels = labels, main="Sales by Province") 

```
```{r}

# Change the seed from 1 to 42, how does it change the plot? Comment the answer 
set.seed(42) 
distr_data <- rnorm(1000, mean=20.5, sd=5.5) 
boxplot(distr_data) 
boxplot(distr_data, notch=TRUE) 

```
```{r}
# histogram example 
hist(distr_data) # change the number of bins to 5 and the border to black, why did the plot change with the number of bins
hist(distr_data, breaks = 20)
```
```{r}
#Change the colour of the plot to purple
d <- density(distr_data)
plot(d, main="Sale Amount Distribution")
polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)),
        c(d$y, rep(0, length(d$y))),
        col = "purple", border = "black")

```
```{r}

library(beeswarm) # plot with default settings 
beeswarm(distr_data) 
# change the orientation to horizontal and the plot points to a hollow triangle
beeswarm(distr_data, pch=2, horizontal = TRUE) 

```
```{r}

# using a built-in dataset 
ToothGrowth$dose <- as.factor(ToothGrowth$dose) 
head(ToothGrowth) # basic plot
p <- ggplot(ToothGrowth, aes(x=dose, y=len)) + geom_violin()
p 
p + geom_boxplot(width=0.1) # add A boxplot with width 0.1 to the beehive 
p + geom_dotplot(binaxis='y', stackdir='center', dotsize=1) 

```
